messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — I'd like to propose a change to admission control for saturated GPU pools. Current behavior (reject) is simple but causing lots of client retries and poor UX. Thinking about a hybrid: try queueing briefly, then fall back to a light degrade, finally reject as last resort. Thoughts?

Samira: +1 to hybrid in principle. Can you share current spike numbers so we can model latency impact?

Alex K: Quick stats from last week (us-west-2 prod pool): GPU util ~92% during peak, queue depth spikes to ~1800 requests, p95 generation latency 450ms, p99 ~1.2s. Error rate (503) increases 4x when we keep rejecting. Clients retry backoff makes thundering herd worse.

Priya R: Rejection is nice for SLA predictability, but for product teams we break flows that expect a response (e.g., interactive chat). Degrade might preserve UX but could cause subtle quality regressions. Need safety net for QA.

Marco: Two concrete degrade options: 1) auto-fallback to a cheaper quantized model variant (same semantics, lower perf cost) 2) reduce max_tokens / sampling budget and stream partial results. Both buy throughput but trade quality.

Alex K: Agree. Proposed policy (config example):
```
admission:
  mode: hybrid
  queue_max_ms: 600
  degrade_after_ms: 600
  degrade_actions:
    - model_fallback: redwood/gpt-xx-q4a
    - max_tokens_factor: 0.6
  reject_after_ms: 2000
```
This means: hold requests in queue up to 600ms, if still cannot start, switch to degrade (model fallback + token cap), if total wait exceeds 2s then reject with 503+Retry-After.

Samira: How do we decide per-tenant? Some customers have reserved capacity (Dedicated) and shouldn't be degraded. Also want priority tiers (committed > paid > dev).

Priya R: We must honor dedicated/reserved flag. Proposal: admission policy evaluates tenant class first, then cluster load. For hosted customers without commitment, allow degraded fallback by default; for dedicated, keep reject-only or full capacity.

Marco: Simulation notes: ran workload replay with hybrid config on a trace of 24h peak. Result: overall 503s dropped by ~70%, average response time increased by ~120ms, cost estimate +5% token-equivalent compute (because fallback model still consumes cycles but less). p99 tail depending on queue_max_ms — if we keep queue_max_ms too high p99 explodes.

Alex K: Good to know cost impact. We should also tie rate-limits to capacity dynamically: token-bucket rate per tenant scaled by pool free tokens. Something like: tenant_qps = min(contract_qps, capacity_share * pool_capacity).

Priya R: Also need observability hooks: per-tenant delta on quality (BLEU/ROUGE-ish evals for generation?) and automated regression alerts when degrade triggers correlate with quality drop.

Samira: Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary in us-west-2 for non-dedicated pools, run for 48h, measure 1) 503 count 2) p95/p99 latency 3) quality regressions on a small eval set 4) cost delta. Also add a circuit-breaker that reverts to reject-only if p99 > 3s or error rate > X.

Marco: Implementation concerns: streaming and partial outputs complicate client SDKs. If we fall back to a different model variant, ensure response schema and function-calling compatibility. We'll need a model-compatibility matrix and automatic transformer.

Alex K: Good point. We can start with simple model_fallback that matches tokenizer/seq semantics. No function-calling for canary initially. Keep degrade limited to text-only endpoints.

ops-bot: rollout: canary "hybrid-admit-v1" enabled in us-west-2 (non-dedicated) at 2026-03-18T18:12:00Z by alexk. Monitoring alert set: infra.admit.hybrid.p99>3s -> auto-disable.

Priya R: Legal/compliance note — for Private/VPC customers we must not change behavior without explicit opt-in. Policy should be opt-in for Private clusters.

Alex K: Action items: 1) Marco to add sim scripts + cost calc (by EOD Friday) 2) Samira to add per-tenant priority rules and circuit-breaker thresholds (PR by Monday) 3) Priya to define minimal eval prompts for canary quality checks (today) 4) Eng-release to schedule canary window and rollback playbook.

Samira: Also let's add a graceful header in degraded responses e.g., X-Redwood-Admit: degraded;reason=model-fallback so clients can adapt.

Alex K: Exactly. Thanks all — will open the RFC PR with config schema and test plan. If no objections in 24h we'll proceed with canary. :thumbsup:
